watches.name: No Mercy
watches.description: Let's be honest. For nearly forty years, we've all been told the same story. Daniel was the hero. Cobra Kai were the villains. But... were they? Hear me out. One kid turns up, gets a few weeks of training, wins the tournament with a lucky (probably illegal) kick and rides off into the sunset. The other guys? They've been training every day. Running laps. Throwing punches. Sweating. Sparring. Living the lifestyle. They're fit. They're disciplined. They turn up on time. Their gis are immaculate. In real life, hard work pays off. Daniel wouldn’t have stood a chance. That idea has inspired Detrash founder Guy Blaskey ever since he first watched the film as a kid in the 1980s. "I've always thought the Cobra Kai aesthetic was unbelievably cool," says Blaskey. "The black uniforms. The confidence. The discipline. Looking back as an adult, I found myself thinking, 'Hang on... these guys actually put the work in… they deserve better!'" That childhood obsession has become No Mercy ; Detrash's newest high-performance dive watch. Finished in stealth black with a black PVD-coated case, black dial and black ocean plastic strap, the watch is punctuated with flashes of red, yellow and white that fans of a certain iconic 1980s dojo might recognise. Limited to 100. No repeats. No re-runs.

watches.name: Field of Dreams
watches.description: The ghosts of watchmakers from the past came to me and said that Detrash needed a field watch. They said to take influences from the past; like the railway minute track from the Dirty Dozen, the twisted lugs from the Polerouter and double-domed sapphire crystal. They said to bring it up to date with a bit of colour, a Miyota 9039 automatic movement, a slim case, a bit of fun text and most importantly eco-friendly materials; a strap made from recycled plastic bottles and a case made from 80% recycled steel. They said to make these in limited batches and put each watch's individual issue number on the back. They said to give a share of each watch sold to eco charities via 1% for the planet. They told me " If you make it, they will come ". Important notes: 1) If the text above sounds like gibberish, you need to watch more 80's Kevin Costner films. There was life before Yellowstone. 2) I made a design choice to use a dark orange lume on the hands, and white lume at 12/3/6/9. This looks great during the day. At night the white glows a lot brighter than the orange. Although it is the best quality Superluminova lume; if you are buying this exclusively to tell the time at night you may be disappointed. The orange does glow, just not that bright. 3) The strap colour is officially khaki. I would describe it as greyish-green. Others might describe is as greenish-grey. Either way it looks great.

watches.name: Au-cean Blue
watches.description: Pronounced "Ocean Blue"... but it's gold and Au is the chemical symbol for gold, so we're being really clever!! Like our McQ; Salmon , the starting point of the design was Steve McQueen's Jaeger-LeCoultre Memovox that he wore in The Thomas Crowne Affair. From there we added some Gerald Genta inspired twisted lugs from the Universal Geneve Polerouter, a few design cues from the Patek Philippe Calatrava, a bit of colour (including a gold PVD coating) and most importantly some 'made from trash' materials. The case is a super slim 8mm (10.6mm with glass), 38mm diameter. It's made from 80% recycled steel. It's mostly brushed, with a hint of high polish. The strap is made from AppleSkin ® - a 'leather' made from fruit juice waste, and lined with soft 'nubuck' made from corn. This is one of the most comfortable watches you will every wear. Scratch-resistant sapphire crystal is used on the front and the exhibition case back, which shows off the Japanese Miyota 9039 movement. These are unlimited editions, made in small batches. Each one is individually numbered on the back, i.e. "Batch 1: 001/100". At least 1% of every sale goes to helping protect the planet. So when you wear it, you’re not just keeping time—you’re part of something bigger.

watches.name: Cali - White
watches.description: The Cali (white) is Detrash's first ever California dial watch, our first watch to have a textured dial, our first watch to feature Cliff (our WWII pilot, surfer, globe mascot) on the dial and our first watch with an exhibition caseback, so you can see the workings of your watch. For those who don't know, a California dial is when you mix Arabic (normal) and Roman numerals. California dial designs date back to the 1930s and were used primarily by Rolex and Panerai. They gained popularity in WWII, as they apparently increase legibility and were known as "error-proof"dials... and most importantly they look great! A 41mm dive watch made with 80% recycled steel, on an ocean-plastic strap, with a Seiko NH35 automatic movement, 200m water resistance and sapphire crystal (front and back). Each watch is limited to 100 pieces, individually numbered and at least 1% of turnover goes to help the planet.

watches.description: Meet Poison Ivy: A bold evolution of the classic dive watch, designed to stand out, built to stand for something. Crafted for everyday wear with a twist of fearless style, Poison Ivy turns heads while treading lightly. The 41mm case is forged from 80% recycled stainless steel and paired with a durable, comfortable ocean-plastic strap, designed to feel good and do good. Powered by the dependable Seiko NH35 automatic movement , its smooth sweeping second hand is a subtle nod to traditional craftsmanship. With sapphire crystal , 200m water resistance, superluminova lume and rugged construction, it's ready for both everyday adventure and deeper dives. Each piece is individually numbered , with only around 100 units produced worldwide . And with at least 1% of every sale supporting environmental causes , Poison Ivy is more than a watch—it’s a statement. Not just built to last. Built to matter.
